items.title: Sammy Penn Interview, 1960-04-21
items.q: But if you do the right thing, Thomas certainly will stick right by you. He'll do that. He's a good leader.

ctx.x: So the next morning was over here early?

So I told him, I says, well, I don't think I am coming back. So he says, well, I talked to Thomas already. He says, now I want to see what you say. I said, well, what did Thomas say? He said, Thomas says, whatever you do is all right. He says, if you come back he'll be glad. I said, well, I says, I want to talk to Thomas first. So I talked to Thomas and he told me, he says, well, if you want to go back it's all right. He says, we'll go back if you go back, if not we won't go back. So I told him, I says, well,…

I mean that helps explain why you all play so well together too. I mean you all work together in every way and stick together. That's right. It's a good unit. A lot of bands aren't that way. They're fighting amongst themselves.

items.title: "Kid Thomas" Valentine Interview, 1964-03-21
items.q: How long have you been with Thomas? About 30 some years. About 32 years.

ctx.x: Well. No. Sammy Penn. Only chance Sammy Penn got. He was on his own. Because I'm a good boy.

Fall off. Yeah. Okay. When were you born? I was born in September. September the 15th. 1902. And where? In Morgan City, Louisiana. And did you play any music out there at all? That's where I started at. I started playing in Morgan City. When I started playing music. It's a funny thing to tell you. What I'm going to tell you. I started. I had one of those cheese boxes. For snare drum. And a white tub. They call it. For a bass drum. And a fellow made me some springs. For a pedal. Made a pedal. That's how I started…

items.title: "Kid Thomas" Valentine Interview, 1959-11-08
items.q: I organized my own band then, you see? That was, that was, I got Edmund Washington, and Sammy, and uh, who was playing bass with us? Bikes?

ctx.x: Most people don't say those things.

No, they ain't got nothing. I'm the only one got them pictures. So, alright. Like, you take like the uniforms. We used to wear a uniform, we had a jacket, a blue jacket, with a dark lapel, you know what I mean? And, blue pants with stripes. And, you know what I mean? None of them fellas don't have the jacket and the pants. I'm still got them. You stayed here? And that been years ago. I even got them white pants we used to wear. Even got that. See? You know what? Sometimes boys see me, we say, man, what? See, they…
Where you live in? He lives out on, oh near Roman Street.

items.title: "Kid Thomas" Valentine Interview, 1959-12-10
items.q: I believe I told Sammy, but Sammy told me he wanted me to get him one

ctx.x: Yeah, they don't use them much.

No, they don't use it no more, but most of them shows used to have, they had to have all that kind of stuff man. Sand paper blocks and all kind of mismaned, the triangle. See the triangle? For walls, that's beautiful. Yeah, that's beautiful. When you're playing the walls, that triangle got different sound. Each fork got a different tone, but it's pretty when you know how to play it, you know what I mean? So, and that's one thing I ain't seen in a long time, but you know one thing? Oh yeah, that's right, I saw a…
Yeah, I used to have one. I don't think I have it anymore, up in Missouri. I'd be, I'd be, I'd be, I'd be, I'd had some triangle there one.
